title: Rank-unimodality of one-descent composition ideals
review: Internal proof and reproducibility review of the preprint.
status: Proof complete within the stated scope.
statement: For every composition with at most one adjacent descent and every bitonic composition, the coefficients counting distinct generalized subwords by total weight are unimodal, with arbitrary weight, part sizes and number of parts. The hosts and coefficients are undilated.
scope_boundary: Vatter’s Conjecture 2.6 for all compositions has wider scope. The paper proves the one-descent case and the bitonic class.
proof_chain: Theorem 2.1 couples weight, number of parts and unused budget on a monotone host at successive budgets. This gives monotonicity for decreasing layer thresholds and log-concavity of the reference cumulative.
Theorem 3.1 and Corollary 3.2 use two comparisons against that reference to prove G_j D_(N-1) >= G_(j-1) D_N on every deletion prefix, N >= 3 and 1 <= j <= N-2.

The hereditary coefficient criterion yields unimodality of the dyadically weighted positive differences of the reversed product for every arm pair. The strict-peak induction proves coefficient unimodality of the core and both relatives.
The greedy distinct-prefix identity identifies the core. Reversal of the right arm, restoration of peak multiplicities and final record parts give the stated hosts.

strict_peak_boundary.algebra: For p=q_X q_Y and W=([M]-z^M)p, (1-z)W=(1-2z^M+z^(M+1))p. For n<M this gives Delta W_n=p_n>=0. Together with deletion on n<b this covers the prefix through max(b,M)-1. At b>M the joining edge starts at b-1>=sigma. At b<=M there is no preceding negative difference.
strict_peak_boundary.interpretation: This proves the boundary step directly for arbitrary arm and peak weights.
